still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, still printed on the box, and still paid by almost nobody.
The FDA has still approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market. Exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the 503B compounding exclusion finalised in 2026 still stands.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance still lets employer wellness programmes tie up to a 30% premium differential to verified adherence or BMI. Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only one in force, and the two EEOC ADA charges are still pending.

The July 2028 class bone and lean-mass warning and the CMS DXA coverage code for users 65+ are unchanged. Tirzepatide's August 2028 dementia-risk label still stands, and its postmarketing confirmatory trial is still running.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 29.6% of ~266M adults is ~78.7M current users. 37.0% ever-used minus 29.6% current = 7.4% of adults who have used the drugs and are off them now. 35% of ever-users have cycled, which is 13.0 points: ~11.0 points are current users on at least their second course (37% of current users, down from 46% because the window added ~15 points of first-time users), and ~2.0 points cycled and are off again. The other ~5.4 points of off-now adults stopped once and have not restarted. That fits one-year persistence improving from about one-third toward ~50% under stable public coverage and $149–199 orals, with ~40% restarting within a year. Age bands (about 53M/88M/61M/64M adults): 9.5M + 26.8M + 24.4M + 17.9M ≈ 78.7M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare 19.0M (24%: 16.6M aged 65+ plus 2.4M disabled under-65), Medicaid 9.0M (11%), commercial 20.3M (26%), legitimate cash via TrumpRx and manufacturer-direct 27.0M (34%), imported or counterfeit 3.4M (4%). Public programmes together are 28.0M (36%), the largest payer category, and Medicare is the largest single payer. Income: the bottom third rose fastest (11→25) through Medicaid opt-ins and $149 orals. The top third rose least (21→33). Its ever-used rate is ~45%, but tapering and 'unmedicated' quitting are visible among upper-income women aged 30–45. Adult obesity is ~33.0%. About 16% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, mostly uninsured working-age adults in the 16 states without Medicaid opt-in and people who tried to start but could not tolerate dose escalation. Under-18 use (~1.3%, ~950k) is still concentrated in ages 12–17 and is now less tilted toward upper-income families because Medicaid covers adolescents in opt-in states.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The Medicare Obesity Treatment Benefit (enacted Jul 2029, effective Oct 2029) adds Part D coverage for BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity, at a statutory net price of $149/month for orals and $245 for injectables, with a $50 copay under the Part D out-of-pocket cap. About 10.2M were enrolled by Dec 2030, ~80% on orals: blend ≈ 0.8×149 + 0.2×245 ≈ $168. 10.2M × $168 × 12 ≈ $20.6B annualised gross. The other ~8.8M Medicare users fill under diabetes, CV, CKD, sleep-apnoea or dementia codes at negotiated prices (semaglutide's negotiated price has been $274 since 2027). CBO score: it assumed an average 9.5M enrollees × $170 × 12 × 10 years ≈ $194B gross, minus ~$40B in beneficiary premiums and cost-sharing and ~$16B in assumed medical offsets ≈ $138B net federal over 2030–2039. That is more than three times the 2027 score of $41B because CBO raised its uptake assumptions. Congress passed it anyway, inside a PBM-reform package whose ~$45B in scored savings covered a third. Medicaid: the same law sets the $149/$245 price for Medicaid and an 85% federal match for obesity coverage. 34 states plus DC cover it, up from 9. 9.0M users × ~$160 blend × 12 ≈ $17.3B/yr, of which ~$14.7B is federal. Two states keep 6- and 12-month adherence/BMI conditions.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $5–35/month with 80+ brands. Canadian generics are CAD 60–95. Generics are approved in ~175 countries. India and China make most of the world's semaglutide by volume, and Chinese generic tirzepatide is now sold in Southeast Asia and the Gulf.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: the Jan 2029 TrumpRx renewal cut oral maintenance doses from $299 to $199. Starting doses stay at $149. Foundayo costs $149–199, Wegovy pens $249, Zepbound vials $249–299, and oral amycretin launched at $299 for the first year under a parity commitment. Retatrutide sits outside the managed channel at ~$449 cash and has little uptake. US cash prices are now ~5–30× Indian generics, down from ~30×. Employer coverage recovered from 44% to 49% as net costs fell, and another 10% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks. BMI ≥35 thresholds and step therapy through orals are standard. Orals are ~58% of all users and ~75% of new starts. Most Medicare and Medicaid starts are on the $149 orals. The gray market (~3.4M users, a falling share) is mostly uninsured adults in non-opt-in states and people buying higher doses than any prescriber will write.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, daily oral (amycretin oral, approved Mar 2030)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2029)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved May 2030)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established cardiovascular disease (tirzepatide, Aug 2028; confirmatory trial ongoing)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'steadiness' / craving-management subscriptions: lowest-dose orals prescribed by telehealth firms and marketed for calm, focus and freedom from craving
alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs; the oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 read out positive in 2030 but is not yet filed
dementia-prevention use by people without cardiovascular disease, cash-paid on orals
nicotine, gambling and compulsive-shopping reduction (observational support only)
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: No new indication this step. Every approval in the window is for chronic weight management, an existing indication. Survodutide's MASH sNDA and oral semaglutide for AUD are both pending or unfiled. The oral_parity driver is realised by oral amycretin: Novo filed it in Feb 2029 on a 72-week head-to-head showing ~20.4% weight loss against injectable tirzepatide's ~20.9%, which met non-inferiority. FDA approved it in Mar 2030, 13 months after filing, so a pill now matches the best-selling injectable. Retatrutide was approved in Mar 2029 after its extended review, with labelled dysesthesia (~9% at top dose) and higher discontinuation. It is the efficacy leader (~26%) but is priced outside managed channels, so uptake is ~0.9M. Survodutide (Boehringer) was approved in May 2030, the first non-Novo, non-Lilly branded incretin for obesity. Injectable amycretin's filing is planned for 2031. MariTide is still not on the US market. Bimagrumab-type muscle-preserving adjuncts are still in phase 2/3 and not approved. Global incretin market ~$150B (2030). US net prices fell ~20–30% while volume roughly doubled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Oral amycretin shows more early nausea than the Wegovy pill. Retatrutide's GI and dysesthesia profile drives its discontinuation.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute case counts are up with the user base; the rate is unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL settlement finalised 2029 without admission.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: No new signal; the 2028 hip-fracture HR ~1.3 for users 65+ after >2 years holds in updated claims. Exposure is what changed: ~16.6M users aged 65+ (up from ~7.5M), most new under the Medicare benefit, so the absolute number exposed has more than doubled. DXA scheduling backlogs run 3–5 months in many regions. Protein-supplement and resistance-training counselling is documented in ~55% of Medicare starts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: July 2028 class warning and CMS DXA code unchanged. The Medicare benefit requires a DXA order within 12 months for women 65+, a requirement that went unfunded beyond the existing code.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflicting; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Unchanged: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA adverse-reactions listing.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2027 cohort figure (~7% vs ~3%) still stands; no new data in the window. Applied to ~78.7M users, that 4-point excess is roughly 3M people with clinically meaningful anhedonia attributable to the drug, if the cohort generalises. The FDA-requested postmarketing study has enrolled but not reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. Telehealth marketing of 'calm' and 'craving freedom' has drawn citizen petitions but no FDA action.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Fewer people are forced to stop now that coverage is steadier.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the Medicare benefit's chronic-therapy design.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Case series continue, especially among low-dose 'steadiness' subscribers eating very little and older Medicare starters.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance only; no label change.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents; effects of repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now. No adolescent bone data have reported yet. Medicaid has widened adolescent exposure.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cumulative FDA reports tied to non-approved product are ~9,800. No cluster since the Feb 2028 contamination event. Mg/unit dosing-error calls to poison centres have plateaued as the gray market's share fell.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert, CBP seizures and state suits against marketplaces continue. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

food_and_beverage.state: About 45% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volume is down ~9% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~8%. Small packs and price increases now recover less of the loss, and dollar sales are down ~2% in real terms. The aesthetic inversion has created a premium niche at the top: full-fat dairy, butcher-counter beef, sourdough and 'unmedicated' indulgence brands sell to upper-income urban buyers, while mass-market lines shrink. Protein is still the growth aisle, now pitched to Medicare-age shoppers after the bone warning.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume is down ~11% from 2025 and beer ~7%. The steadiness subscriptions reach moderate drinkers, not only heavy ones. Distillers keep consolidating US capacity and push exports. Craft cocktail bars in Brooklyn and Austin market 'appetite hours' to off-drug crowds, but that does not offset losses in mid-sized cities.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Chains run permanent half-portion menus, and senior-discount early dinners shrank as Medicare starts surged. High-end restaurants split: 'hunger dinners' (long tasting menus that require arriving with an appetite) became a status booking in New York, Los Angeles and Austin, while mid-tier casual dining takes the volume hit.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep closing stores. The new pressure comes from the top: 'built' fits with a broader chest and thigh, and fewer size-0 lines at premium brands. Thinness alone no longer sells in premium womenswear marketing. Rental and stretch still serve cyclers.

fitness.state: Strength training dominates. Body-composition scanning chains grew with the Medicare DXA requirement. Natural bodybuilding federations' new GLP-1 testing created an 'unmedicated' competitive category, and upscale gyms market drug-free strength cohorts. Silver-strength classes for Medicare starters are the volume growth.

insurance.state: Employer pharmacy trend fell to ~+6% as net prices dropped, and coverage recovered to 49%, still mostly behind prior authorisation and BMI thresholds. Employers with many workers over 65 shift those users to Medicare. Part D plan bids for 2030 rose ~11%, about half of it from the obesity benefit. Monitored metabolic tracks persist at ~3.5M enrollees. PBMs lost some rebate income under the reform package.

pharma.state: Volume roughly doubled while US net prices fell 20–30%. Lilly and Novo still hold ~93% of US branded incretin revenue, and Boehringer entered with survodutide. Orals are the main revenue line. Medicare is the largest single customer. Both majors are positioning for the 2031–32 exclusivity cliff with next-generation orals and the amycretin franchise.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A lean, soft body no longer signals money. It reads as Medicare, Medicaid or a $149 pill. Among upper-income urban professionals, visible muscle with a little softness, eating in public and an 'unmedicated' claim now carry status. A regained body still reads as lapsed coverage in middle-income workplaces, but less often, because coverage lapses less.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class sign has flipped at the top and held at the bottom. In Manhattan, Los Angeles and Austin, upper-income women aged 30–45 taper off publicly, post 'first hungry month' diaries and pay trainers to rebuild. Lower-income and older Americans gained thinness through public coverage just as it stopped being scarce. 'Unmedicated vitality' is the new scarce body: it takes time, food, trainers and the freedom to go without the drug's benefits. Natural bodybuilding federations now test for GLP-1s, and 'certified unmedicated' badges appear on dating and fitness profiles.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Most households have someone not hungry at the table, so shared meals are shorter and often staggered. At the top, appetite has become performance: long hunger dinners, ostentatious bread, Sunday roasts posted as proof of being off. The Tulsa-born 'Bread Alone' fasting network claims ~700 congregations and frames itself as the discipline both camps lack.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles carry 'on', 'off' or 'unmedicated'. 'Unmedicated' is a premium signal on upscale apps and a red flag on others ('too intense'). Desire mismatch is still a top presenting issue for couples therapists, and synchronised dosing is common among older couples who both enrolled through Medicare.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Clinics, Medicare and employers still treat appetite as noise to be regulated. Among the affluent and the art world, appetite has been re-scarcified as evidence of vitality and inner life. The counter-movement grew more fashionable and less political: the Unmuted collective now has Austin and Los Angeles chapters and a brand-sponsorship problem.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically measured anhedonia still rests on the 2027 cohort (~7% vs ~3%). At ~78.7M users that implies ~3M excess cases if it generalises. A much larger group, perhaps a third of users in vendor surveys, describe 'evenness'. Telehealth firms now sell that evenness directly: ~4.5M adults are in low-dose 'steadiness' subscriptions ($149/month cash for lowest-dose orals), counted within the cash-pay users.
interior_life.framing: Sold as a product. Telehealth brands (Ro's 'Even', Hims & Hers' 'Quiet') advertise 'calm, focus, freedom from craving' on subway posters and podcasts without naming a molecule, a tactic that keeps them clear of manufacturer off-label promotion rules. Clinicians still call it a side effect. Unmuted calls it sedation for sale. Users call it 'being even'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Steady' appears in job postings at call centres and logistics firms. Remote knowledge workers buy steadiness subscriptions as focus aids, the way earlier cohorts used modafinil, and some employers reimburse them through wellness stipends rather than health plans, outside the adherence-premium rules. Monitored metabolic tracks hold at ~3.5M enrollees. The two EEOC charges are still undecided, and California's premium bill stalled in committee.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down again. Comedy promoters complain about quieter rooms in commuter suburbs. 'Off nights' became a scene: Unmuted's Brooklyn and Austin events sell out and draw brand money, which splits the collective. 'Flat' fiction has a backlash genre of appetite memoirs. Video-game studios report longer, calmer play sessions and less in-game spending among identifiable users.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is common. Steadiness subscribers report fewer fights and less sex in roughly equal measure. Some couples treat drug holidays as a romance ritual, which keeps cycling going even among people whose coverage is secure.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2028–29 coalition split over Medicare. MAHA-aligned legislators and fat-acceptance groups opposed the benefit, while seniors' groups, labour and most Republicans in swing districts backed it, and it passed. The anti-premium coalition kept its Illinois win but lost momentum. Pundits now claim 'calm' subscriptions dampen protest, but there is no turnout or protest-count evidence for it.

state.regulatory_posture: No new regulatory action this step. FDA approved retatrutide, survodutide and oral amycretin on ordinary review timelines, issued no new warnings and has not acted on telehealth 'steadiness' marketing despite citizen petitions. Import posture is unchanged: rhetoric, alerts, seizures, porous personal importation.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The expansion came through the coverage driver, not new conditioning rules. Congress enacted the Medicare Obesity Treatment Benefit and the Medicaid enhanced match (Jul 2029) at statutory prices of $149 for orals and $245 for injectables. No mandate. The 2027 tri-agency wellness guidance is unchanged.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in kind. PBM fill data and app-linked logs feed employer metabolic tracks (~3.5M enrollees). Two Medicaid programmes keep their 6- and 12-month adherence/BMI conditions, now applied to a much larger enrolled population. The Medicare benefit itself has no adherence condition beyond standard refill data.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules and the Army recruit oral pilot are unchanged. DOT still has not ruled on off-label alcohol-reduction use by truckers. Some federal contractors reimburse steadiness subscriptions under wellness stipends.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China remain the world's volume source. The US–India trade framework includes CBP cooperation on mail-order vials. With US cash prices down to $149–199, the Danish–US price row has cooled. Manufacturers point to the statutory Medicare price as proof of their US concessions in tariff talks.

events.event: TrumpRx renewal: Novo and Lilly cut oral maintenance doses from $299 to $199 and top-dose injectables to $249–299 in exchange for tariff treatment. $149 starting doses held.

Congress passes the Medicare Obesity Treatment Benefit and a Medicaid enhanced match inside a PBM-reform package. Statutory prices are $149 for orals and $245 for injectables, with a $50 copay. CBO scores it at ~$138B net over ten years. Enrolment opens in October.
Ro launches 'Even', a $149/month low-dose oral subscription advertised for 'calm, focus and freedom from craving'. Rivals follow, and steadiness subscriptions pass 4 million adults by late 2030.

FDA approves oral amycretin after a head-to-head trial finds it non-inferior to injectable tirzepatide (~20.4% vs ~20.9%). A pill now matches the leading injectable, and orals reach three-quarters of new starts.
Two natural bodybuilding federations add GLP-1 testing and an 'unmedicated' division. 'Certified unmedicated' badges spread to dating apps and upscale gyms in New York, Los Angeles and Austin.

open_tensions: Medicare is now the largest single payer, for ~16.6M users aged 65+, the age group the 2028 bone warning says is most harmed. DXA backlogs run months, and the benefit's ten-year cost assumes prices that the 2031–32 exclusivity cliff will either lower or that manufacturers will fight to hold.

Blunting is sold as 'calm' to ~4.5M subscribers at the lowest doses, while the FDA's postmarketing study has not reported and ~3M excess anhedonia cases are implied. The EEOC charges and the stalled California bill leave the line between product, side effect and employment condition undrawn.

The body's class sign has inverted: thinness is now the look of public coverage, and 'unmedicated vitality' is a luxury good. Some upper-income users taper off while public programmes medicate the bottom third, and nobody knows whether that is a health gradient or a fashion.
Medicaid expansion has widened adolescent exposure beyond the upper-income cohort, still with no bone data, during the years when peak bone mass forms.

prose.headline: The Cheap Body: Thin Became the Medicare Look, So the Rich Started Eating Again
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 nearly three American adults in ten take an incretin drug every day, and most of them take it as a pill. The needle is gone as an argument. In March the FDA approved oral amycretin after a head-to-head trial showed it doing almost exactly what an injectable tirzepatide does, and three-quarters of new patients now start on a tablet. The $1,349 list price is still printed on Wegovy boxes. It is a museum label. Starting doses still cost $149 through the government's cash channel, maintenance has fallen to $199, and the injectables top out under $300.

The bigger change is who pays. Congress balked at the bill in 2027, then passed something larger in 2029, after the Bridge pilot's lapse sent half a million older patients back to regaining and after it became clear Medicare was already paying through the dementia label. The new Medicare obesity benefit sets a statutory price, $149 for pills and $245 for pens, with a $50 copay. Ten million beneficiaries enrolled within fifteen months. Another nine million fill under heart, kidney, diabetes and dementia codes. Thirty-four states took the matching Medicaid offer. Public programmes now pay for more of these prescriptions than employers do, and Medicare is the largest single customer Novo and Lilly have. CBO put the decade's cost at about $138 billion, more than three times its earlier score, because it finally assumed people would use the drugs.

So a body the drug made lean no longer says anything about money. In middle-income offices it says nothing much. In Manhattan, Los Angeles and Austin it says Medicare, or Medicaid, or a $149 pill. The affluent have moved on to what cannot be prescribed: muscle, time, a trainer, an appetite shown in public. Upper-income women in their thirties and forties post diaries of their first hungry month off the drug. Tasting menus that require you to arrive hungry are the hardest reservations in town. Two natural bodybuilding federations now test for semaglutide, and 'certified unmedicated' badges have migrated onto dating profiles. Nobody knows yet whether this is a health choice or a fashion, and the people doing it don't much care.

The drug's quieter effect is now sold openly. Telehealth firms advertise lowest-dose pills for 'calm, focus, freedom from craving' without naming a molecule, and about four and a half million adults pay $149 a month for that evenness. Remote workers use it the way an earlier cohort used modafinil, and some employers reimburse it as a wellness stipend. The 2027 cohort that found clinically meaningful flattening of pleasure in seven percent of users, against three percent of non-users, has not been superseded. At this scale that gap is about three million people. The FDA's follow-up study has not reported.

The older users are the open question. The bone and muscle warning from 2028 still stands, and the hip-fracture hazard has not moved. What moved is exposure: more than sixteen million people over sixty-five are now on the drugs, and DXA scans that Medicare requires for older women are booked three to five months out in much of the country. Silver-strength classes are the fastest-growing line at gyms that pulled their treadmills two years ago.

The industries kept adapting. Snack volume is down nearly a tenth from 2025 and price increases no longer cover it. Spirits keep shrinking as the calm subscriptions reach moderate drinkers. Premium butchers and full-fat dairy sell to people proving they can eat. The mail still brings Indian vials to three and a half million Americans, mostly uninsured adults in states that declined the Medicaid match, though fewer each quarter as the price gap narrows. The generics cliff arrives in 2031. Everyone is pricing for it already.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Arredondo, sixty-seven, takes her pill at 6:10 with a full glass of water and then waits the thirty minutes, standing at the kitchen window in Dayton watching the school buses she used to dispatch. The box says $1,349. The pharmacy charged her fifty.

At nine she drives to the strip mall where the DXA place opened next to a vape shop that closed. The appointment card from March says September. She asks if there were cancellations. The receptionist, who is maybe twenty-five and visibly muscular, says no and hands her a protein-shake coupon.

Lunch is half a turkey sandwich. She wraps the other half for Ray, who is on his pill too. They synchronised in October, both enrolled the first week, and they eat together at five now, early, small, mostly quiet.

Her daughter calls from Columbus on her break. Marisol is on something called Even, $149 a month, no insurance involved, for the call-centre job. 'I just don't get mad anymore, Mom.' Denise says that's good. It sounds good.

At three she goes to the senior strength class at the gym, which is mostly women her age holding kettlebells like grocery bags. The instructor says 'protect your hips' four times.

In the evening, her granddaughter's dating profile is open on Ray's iPad, left there from FaceTime. Under her photo, holding a barbell: certified unmedicated.

'What's that supposed to mean,' Ray says.

Denise looks at it a while. She isn't hungry. She hasn't been hungry since October. She closes the cover.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Part D plan bids for 2030 rose ~11%, about half of it from the obesity benefit.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: Part D bids for 2030 are filed in early June 2029, before the July 2029 enactment of the Medicare benefit, so the benefit could not be priced into them. The causal chain is chronologically impossible as stated.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The class sign has flipped at the top and held at the bottom.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the world's own figures put the top income third at 33% current use and ~45% ever-used. The 'flip' rests on a niche of tapering upper-income women in three cities and two bodybuilding federations, so a two-year class-sign reversal is asserted rather than shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo filed it in Feb 2029 on a 72-week head-to-head showing ~20.4% weight loss against injectable tirzepatide's ~20.9%
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: amycretin was only in phase 3 in mid-2028, so a completed 72-week head-to-head against tirzepatide filed by Feb 2029 needs a trial started by about autumn 2027. An oral peptide hitting ~20% is also very optimistic, though the driver stipulates the parity itself.

rationale.badness: Access, price and inequality improve on 2028: Medicare and Medicaid expansion and $149 orals narrow the income gap and cut regain-after-lapse. The costs are the 65+ exposure to the unchanged ~1.3 hip-fracture hazard (16.6M users, DXA backlogs of 3–5 months), ~4.5M people in 'steadiness' subscriptions with ~3M implied excess anhedonia cases and no FDA action, and widened adolescent exposure without bone data. Epistemic is the worst dimension, because the blunting is sold unnamed, the postmarketing study has not reported, and the 3.5M in employer-monitored tracks persists. Overall it is a harder society in some respects and a fairer one in others, not a collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised: the adoption delta (29.6%), managed decline ($299 to $199 in the Jan 2029 TrumpRx renewal), public expansion (Medicare benefit and Medicaid match), oral parity (oral amycretin), aesthetic inversion, and marketed 'steadiness'. The no-new-indication, no-safety-signal, no-shock and no-state-action drivers are respected, and the approvals fit the rules. mechanism: The Medicare and Medicaid chain is well shown (Bridge lapse, CBO re-score, PBM package), but the Part D 2030 bid claim is chronologically impossible, the aesthetic-inversion shifts in apparel and class status are asserted from thin evidence, and the oral amycretin trial timeline is tight (claims 1–3). magnitude: Population figures sit inside the envelope, and age bands, payer mix (78.7M), Medicare ($20.6B, CBO $194B to $138B), Medicaid ($17.3B, $14.7B federal) and the 950k pediatric figure all reconcile. Approval timing for retatrutide, survodutide and oral amycretin is lawful; the only small slips are 4M vs 4.5M subscribers and the amycretin trial-timing squeeze.
rationale.generativity: The prose supplies a concrete day for Denise: the 30-minute wait, the DXA appointment card that says September, synchronised dosing with Ray, her daughter on 'Even', and the 'certified unmedicated' badge on a granddaughter's profile. The world fields add a lot of texture: hunger dinners, silver-strength classes, off nights, and 'Quiet' and 'Even' subway ads. Several scenes are implied in the fields, and the vignette shows rather than explains.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Public programmes together are 28.0M (36%), the largest payer category, and Medicare is the largest single payer.
least_plausible_claims.why: The candidate's own payer mix puts Medicare at 19.0M users, below commercial at 20.3M and legitimate cash at 27.0M. Medicare is not the largest single payer by users, and the dollar figures don't support it either. This is a magnitude reconciliation failure, and the prose repeats it as 'the largest single customer'.

least_plausible_claims.quote: minus ~$40B in beneficiary premiums and cost-sharing and ~$16B in assumed medical offsets ≈ $138B net federal over 2030–2039
least_plausible_claims.why: The stated $50 monthly copay on about 9.5M average enrollees comes to roughly $5.7B a year, or about $57B over ten years. That alone exceeds the $40B deducted for premiums and cost-sharing combined, so the $138B net does not follow from the stated inputs. This fails magnitude.

least_plausible_claims.quote: That fits one-year persistence improving from about one-third toward ~50% under stable public coverage and $149–199 orals, with ~40% restarting within a year.
